title: Slay the Spire 2
release_date: full release not yet (Early Access; Mega Crit says EA will last until it 'feels right', likely ~1–2 years); PC (Steam) only so far
developer: Mega Crit (founders Anthony Giovannetti and Casey Yano)
team_size: core team of ~10 people plus contributors (remote) [CONFIRMED in substance – PCGamesN/GeekWire, re-confirmed in a cross-check search on 2026-10-08]; an 8-person crew ran the Oct 2023 Godot test jam ('Dancing Duelists') [secondary source case study]
developer_background: Second game. Slay the Spire (EA 2017, full 2019) effectively defined the roguelike deckbuilder genre and sold millions; Mega Crit is also a publisher (Mega Crit Games label). StS2 was in development ~2 years in Unity before the studio switched to Godot after Unity's Sept 2023 runtime-fee announcement; game revealed at the Triple-I Initiative showcase in April 2024. Mega Crit is a major Godot Foundation sponsor.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2868840/Slay_the_Spire_2/ (Windows/macOS/Linux; Steam Deck). No console version during EA.
business_model: premium Early Access $24.99 (no launch discount; Steam page says the price will increase after EA); bundles with Slay the Spire and with Dispatch
units_or_downloads: 3,000,000+ units in the first week (~3.3M; '25M runs attempted') [CONFIRMED – Mega Crit Steam post via GosuGamers/Gamereactor/FullCleared, ~2026-03-12]. Later third-party Steam estimates: 4.6M by 2026-03-19, 5.3M by end of March, 6.5M by 2026-05-14, 7.1M by 2026-07-09 [ESTIMATE – Alinea Analytics via Wccftech/Insider Gaming/FRVR]; 7.4M paid units [ESTIMATE – VG Insights, ~Sept/Oct 2026]; ~6.2M [ESTIMATE – Raijin, Sept 2026]. No official update after week 1 found.
peak_concurrent_players: 574,638 on Steam during first weekend (~2026-03-07/08) [CONFIRMED – SteamDB/SteamCharts data via GosuGamers; Tracker.gg shows 574,377]. Top-20 all-time Steam peak, ~12.5k short of Silksong's 587,150. Monthly avg CCU fell from ~279k (March) to ~64k (last 30 days, ~Sept 2026) [SteamCharts].
steam_reviews: ~201,000 reviews, 61% positive ('Mixed'/'Mostly Positive' boundary) [Raijin, Sept 2026]; Steam locale snapshots show 142k–151k at 62–63% all languages (undated, ~spring/summer 2026); English-only ~70.6k at 91% (earlier snapshot); VG Insights 57.6% positive. Score fell from Overwhelmingly Positive to Mixed after review-bomb waves in March 2026 (10,000+ negative reviews on 2026-03-20 alone) over balance nerfs to infinite combos/'Prepared' and the Act 3 boss Doormaker, partly on a beta branch; Mega Crit rolled back several nerfs.
implied_review_multiplier: ~31–37 [ESTIMATE – tracker units (Raijin 6.2M / VG Insights 7.4M) ÷ ~201k reviews, Sept 2026]; no confirmed unit figure exists at a date with a known review count. Inflated review count from the review bomb pushes this ratio down.
gross_revenue: ≈ $133M Steam gross by July 2026 [ESTIMATE – 7.1M Alinea units × $18.74 avg realised price ($24.99 × 0.75)]. Tracker figures: $108M by end of March 2026 and $141.7M by 2026-07-09 [ESTIMATE – Alinea Analytics]; $147M [ESTIMATE – VG Insights]; $92.4M lifetime [ESTIMATE – Raijin, Sept 2026].
net_revenue: ≈ $96M to Mega Crit [ESTIMATE – $133M gross; Steam tiered cut (30% first $10M, 25% $10–50M, 20% above) leaves $103.5M × 0.93 refunds = $96.2M]. Self-published, so no publisher split. Range ≈ $75–103M depending on tracker gross.
production_cost: ≈ $3.5–6M [ESTIMATE – ~10 core staff × ~57 months (dev from ~mid-2021 to EA March 2026) × $6k/month ≈ $3.4M, plus contractors (art, music, porting, localisation) and US-salary premium; no disclosed figure]. Funded from Slay the Spire profits.
development_time: ~4.5–5 years to Early Access [ESTIMATE – Mega Crit said it had spent 'over two years' in Unity by Sept 2023 (start ≈ mid-2021); engine switch to Godot ~Oct 2023; EA 2026-03-05]. EA expected to last ~1–2 years more.
why_popular: Sequel to the genre-defining roguelike deckbuilder (huge, loyal, streamer-friendly fanbase); same 'one more run' loop with new characters, cards, relics and co-op multiplayer; extremely high wishlist-to-sales conversion; $24.99 price; Steam-only launch concentrated all players in one store so it topped Steam's March 2026 best-seller chart above AAA releases (Crimson Desert, Resident Evil Requiem, Marathon). Strong Twitch/YouTube watchability (decision-heavy runs).
marketing_channels: Reveal at Triple-I Initiative showcase (April 2024); trailers; years of wishlists from the original's fanbase; heavy Twitch/YouTube streamer coverage (original StS is a staple streamer game); Steam front page/top seller; Discord/Reddit community; no paid UA reported. Godot narrative also earned extra tech-press coverage.
engine: Godot 4 [CONFIRMED – Mega Crit statements and SteamDB tech listing; switched from Unity after the Sept 2023 runtime-fee controversy, via a 3-week Godot prototype jam in Oct 2023]
art_style: 2D hand-painted/illustrated cards and characters with skeletal (puppet) animation, stylised dark-fantasy UI, clean readable card frames
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write nearly all deckbuilder logic in Godot (card/relic effect system, turn manager, map generation, enemy intents, save/run history, data-driven content tables), generate card art and enemy illustrations, card text variants, SFX and music. Turn-based single-player 2D is one of the most AI-friendly genres. | AI cannot: do the part that made StS great – card-pool design, synergy depth, balance across hundreds of cards (StS2's own review bomb shows how sensitive balance is), enemy intent design, run pacing, art-style consistency across 100+ illustrations, and thousands of hours of playtesting. Co-op multiplayer adds sync complexity. Scoring 4 not 5 because a competitive deckbuilder needs large content plus long balancing; a small 'StS-like' MVP is fast, but reaching StS quality is not. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 + GodotSteam; Midjourney/Scenario (style-locked LoRA) for card art; Spine/Godot Skeleton2D for puppet animation; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno/Udio music; Python simulation scripts (Claude-written) for automated balance testing.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, $150–$500 (1 character, ~60–80 cards, 20 relics, 1 act with 10–15 enemies + 1 boss; Claude Pro/Max, image gen, Steam Direct $100)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 6–12 months, $3,000–$12,000 (3 characters, ~250 cards, 3 acts; freelance art cleanup/consistency pass $1.5–6k, composer $1–3k, localisation, playtest/marketing + Next Fest demo; excludes developer's own living costs)

data_conflicts: Peak CCU: 'nearly 600,000' (gamesmarket.global/Insider Gaming) vs exact 574,638 (SteamDB via GosuGamers/SteamCharts) – used 574,638. Week-1 units: 'over 3M' vs '3.3M' in headlines – used 3M+ as the confirmed floor. The Sensor Tower '~7M' lead could not be tied to a source in this session; Alinea's 7.1M (2026-07-09) and VG Insights' 7.4M are consistent with it, while Raijin is lower (6.2M units, $92.4M). Review score: English-only snapshot 91% vs all-language 57–63% after the March 2026 review bombs – reported both. Team size: '~10 core + contributors' (PCGamesN/GeekWire) vs a blog claiming a 'two-person studio' (refers to the founders) – used ~10.
notes: Biggest roguelike-deckbuilder launch ever on Steam. Lessons: (1) Godot is now proven for a 500k+ CCU commercial hit, which matters for solo devs avoiding Unity licensing risk. (2) Balance changes in Early Access can trigger review bombs even on a beta branch; communicate patch intent clearly and use opt-in betas. (3) The deckbuilder format is very AI-friendly to build but content/balance-heavy; budget most time for design iteration and automated balance simulation.
